title: compat: implement Responses API v2 variants, deterministic seed passthrough, and streaming reassembly fixes
author: Anita Kapoor
release_notes: Adds OpenAI Responses API v2-style compatibility: response_mode variants, deterministic seed passthrough, improved streaming chunk reassembly, and enhanced function-calling/structured output mapping. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in via 'openai_compat_v2' flag.
commits: a1d4f3c: initial compatibility shim for Responses v2, add response_mode and seed passthrough
b7c9e21: streaming reassembly: boundary-aware buffering and out-of-order chunk handling; add unit tests
f2e6b7a: structured-output: map 'response_format' schema to internal verifier, update tool-calling mapping and docs
description:
Context: Customers expect parity with newer OpenAI Responses API variants (v2-like semantics) and rely on a combination of features: explicit response_mode choices (sync, async_stream), deterministic seeds/seeded sampling for reproducible outputs, metadata passthrough to downstream logs, and richer structured-output/function-calling semantics. This PR implements a compatibility layer that maps OpenAI-style request fields to Redwood's existing inference runtime and adds stability fixes for streaming events.

Motivation: several enterprise integrations and the new response gateway require deterministic replay for evals (ENG-8421) and robust streaming under high concurrency (ENG-8430).

Design summary:
1) Request mapping: introduce openai_compat_v2 enabled via API config. When enabled, we accept top-level fields response_mode (values: "response_stream" | "complete"), seed (integer) and deterministic (boolean). These are translated into an internal sampling profile (seed -> RNG seed; deterministic=true pins temperature=0 and disables sampling path where appropriate). Metadata passthrough: any top-level "metadata" object is preserved and attached to the inference event envelope as metadata.passthrough for audit logs and Console tracing.

2) Tool/Function calling: add support for OpenAI-style "function_call" options (none/auto/manual) and map the function schema into Redwood's StructuredOutput verifier. We implement a permissive-to-strict mode: permissive will accept best-effort JSON and attach parse warnings; strict validates against provided schema and fails fast.

3) Streaming reassembly: previously, multi-part SSE/chunked stream messages occasionally produced truncated JSON frames at high concurrency because the kernel-level socket boundaries didn't align with token boundaries. We implemented boundary-aware buffering: each stream fragment is annotated with sequence_id and offset by the runtime; reassembly tolerates reordered fragments (up to 3 slots) and yields partial deltas only when a JSON token boundary is complete. This reduces spurious parse failures and reduces duplicate partial-emit events.

4) Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged. The compatibility layer is opt-in via either a per-account feature flag or a per-request header X-Redwood-Compat: openai_v2. Migration notes and opt-in progression are included in docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Add OpenAI request field parsing + mapping
- [x] Implement seed -> RNG passthrough and determinism bindings
- [x] Implement function_call mapping and structured-output verifier
- [x] Implement streaming reassembly algorithm and unit tests
- [x] Add CI tests that mimic OpenAI-style streaming deltas and function-call flows
- [x] Docs and changelog updates
- [x] Manual canary on dedicated cluster for 48h

Tests & CI: added integration test suite under integrations/openai_compat that simulates response_stream with interleaved tool messages, seeded sampling reproducibility tests (seed X produces identical outputs over 5 runs), and structured-output schema validation tests. Local lint and unit tests pass; full CI green: 18/18 checks.

Files changed (high level):
- api/openai_compat/bridge.py: main mapping layer and feature-flag gate
- runtime/streaming/reassembly.py: new boundary-aware reassembler and tests
- runtime/sampling/seed_manager.py: seed passthrough and deterministic toggle
- runtime/structured_output/verifier.py: schema mapping and permissive/strict modes
- integrations/openai_compat/*: test harness and fixtures
- docs/openai_compat.md: migration and API examples
- sdk/python/openai_compat_examples.py: example request payloads
- infra/ci/openai_compat.yml: new CI job and quotas

Notes on behaviour differences:
- seed semantics: we map OpenAI's integer seed directly to the RNG state used by our sampling backend. When deterministic=true we force deterministic sampling where the runtime supports it; however on quantized kernels that internally rely on nondeterministic GPU ops absolute bitwise parity is not guaranteed, so we surface a warning in response.metadata when perfect bitwise repeatability is not attainable.

- Streaming: We expose a new header X-Redwood-Stream-Seq for advanced clients that want low-level ordering guarantees; typical clients do not need this.

- Function calling: We intentionally keep a permissive mode to reduce breakages for existing clients that rely on embedding-tool glue.

Review summary:
- Ethan Liu (approve): asked for clearer docs on when deterministic guarantees cannot be fully met on certain hardware; added note and metadata warning.
- Priya Nair (request changes -> approved): requested additional unit tests for out-of-order stream fragments and suggested reducing reorder tolerance from 5 slots to 3; updated implementation accordingly.
- Samir Patel (comment): noted an edge-case where metadata keys overlapping with reserved runtime keys could be overwritten; added namespacing to passthrough payload.

Post-merge actions:
- Schedule a Dedicated-canary rollout on release/next-stable for 48h with opt-in header for customers.
- Monitoring: added traces and dashboards in Console (per-request metadata, stream parse failures, seed-repeatability-violations) and an alert if stream parse failures exceed 0.05% over 15m.

Related: ENG-8421 (deterministic evals), ENG-8430 (streaming stability), DEP-1012 (structured-output schema formats). Thanks to the runtime and infra teams for pairing on the reassembly algorithm and to SDK leads for example payloads.
